description: F-4E Phantom II displayed in the outdoor park of the Sacred Defence museum garden. It wears the serial 3-5614 but the contributor database flags this as a marking rather than a confirmed identity, so the tail number is left blank. Iranian F-4Es were the backbone of the 1980-88 air war.
museum_name: Museum of the Islamic Revolution and Holy Defence

description: Two-seat MiG-21U-600, c/n 664617. The museum presents it as an aircraft captured from Iraqi forces, and Iranian state media repeated that in July 2025; the construction number recorded by the contributor database instead ties the airframe to an ex-East German air force machine numbered 288. The two accounts cannot both be right, the aircraft carries Iranian air force colours with no markings, and the tail number is therefore left blank.
museum_name: Museum of the Islamic Revolution and Holy Defence

description: Captured Iraqi Air Force Su-22UM3K two-seater, serial 22533, held as a war trophy. A visitor comment on the source database records that only the fuselage survives and suggests the sub-type is more properly Su-22UM-4K.
museum_name: Museum of the Islamic Revolution and Holy Defence
